card.decision: Should longest_word return the word in its original casing, or the lower-cased form that words() produces?

experts.why: P-reuse says reuse words() rather than rewrite it.
Acceptable if the docstring states the lower-cased return; the implementation already keeps it.
Reusing words() is the simplest path; a test pins the casing so it cannot change by accident.
Shipping with the existing helper is the smallest change; casing can be added if users ask.

options.consequence: Reuses words() unchanged; the return value differs from the spelling in the input. Documented in the docstring and pinned by a test. Can be changed later, but callers relying on it would break.
options.label: Return the lower-cased word

options.consequence: Needs a way to recover the original token, either a new tokenising path or a change to words(), which is shared with word_count. Touches P-reuse; more code and tests.
options.label: Return the original casing

ticket.purpose: Add a new module `src/longest.py` with `longest_word(text)` returning the longest word in `text`. Reuse the existing `words` helper from `src/textstats.py`.
ticket.title: Add longest_word

card.while_waiting: This ticket is parked at plan; other tickets continue.
card.why: src/textstats.py words() calls text.lower() before splitting, so longest_word('Hello') would return 'hello' if reused unchanged. The ticket says to reuse words(), but it does not say whether the caller expects the spelling from the source text.
